 Wake Forest has never been ranked higher than No. 10 in the AP poll. Stacy Revere / Getty Images 
 By Matt Brown Nov. 15, 2026 10:35 am EST Updated Share article 14 The latest AP Top 25 college football rankings will be revealed around 2 p.m. ET Monday, delayed a day because of the postponement of No. 19 Ole Miss at Oklahoma to Sunday. Check back Monday for the updated poll, as well as ballot analysis from The Athletic’s voter, Ralph Russo. 
 Another eventful weekend in college football featured each of the top 12 teams in the AP poll winning but eight of the next 13 losing — with Ole Miss still to play Oklahoma on Sunday. What will the delayed rankings look like on Monday after a weekend that thinned the College Football Playoff bubble ? Let’s break down the impending movement.
 AP Top 25 results in Week 11 Rank Team Record Result 
 1 Georgia 9-1 W 48-21 vs. Missouri 
 2 Utah 10-0 W 40-39 at No. 22 Arizona 
 3 Notre Dame 9-1 W 41-7 vs. Boston College 
 4 UCLA 10-0 W 22-14 vs. Illinois 
 5 Miami 9-1 W 36-25 vs. Duke 
 6 Indiana 9-1 W 27-13 vs. No. 15 USC 
 7 Alabama 8-2 W 21-6 at Vanderbilt 
 8 Texas 8-2 W 22-21 at No. 24 LSU 
 9 Tennessee 8-2 W 22-7 at Texas A&M 
 10 Texas Tech 9-1 W 52-27 at Oklahoma State 
 11 Wake Forest 9-1 W 49-7 at No. 25 SMU 
 12 BYU 8-2 W 28-7 vs. Baylor 
 13 Kentucky 7-3 L 21-14 vs. Florida 
 14 Houston 7-3 L 42-32 at Colorado 
 15 USC 7-3 L 27-13 at No. 6 Indiana 
 16 Iowa 8-2 W 28-7 vs. Purdue 
 17 Boise State 9-1 W 46-41 vs. Oregon State 
 18 Oregon 7-3 W 31-7 vs. Michigan 
 19 Ole Miss 6-3 TBD 
 20 South Carolina 6-4 L 34-6 at Arkansas 
 21 Ohio State 7-3 W 28-19 vs. Northwestern 
 22 Arizona 7-3 L 40-39 vs. No. 2 Utah 
 23 New Mexico 8-2 L 21-17 vs. UNLV 
 24 LSU 6-4 L 22-21 vs. No. 8 Texas 
 25 SMU 7-3 L 49-7 vs. No. 11 Wake Forest 
 Will there be a shuffle at the top?
 It’s hard to see much movement after the top 12 teams went 12-0. Georgia, which received 53 of 70 first-place votes last week, isn’t going to loosen its grip on No. 1 after dominating Missouri. No. 2 Utah (12 first-place votes) won a shootout at No. 22 Arizona by a point, and No. 3 Notre Dame (five first-place votes) took care of business against Boston College in a game that won’t move the needle.
 Advertisement
 I’d expect at least the top eight to stay the same, though No. 6 Indiana — ranked two spots ahead of where it’s at in the CFP Top 25 — could pick up some voting points after beating No. 15 USC by two touchdowns , allowing it to gain ground on UCLA and Miami.
 Of the top 12 teams, the one to watch is No. 11 Wake Forest , which dominated No. 25 SMU 49-7 on the road and is starting to attract more attention. Jumping over No. 10 Texas Tech wouldn’t be surprising.
 The Demon Deacons have never finished in the top 10, and they’ve never been ranked higher than No. 10 in any AP poll, period. They probably won’t jump No. 9 Tennessee this week, but the highest ranking in program history is within reach.
 Who’s rising and falling?
 Iowa lacks marquee wins but is going to keep sneaking up, perhaps as high as No. 13. Boise State, the clear Group of 6 favorite for the Playoff, will keep creeping up after beating Oregon State. And preseason No. 2 Oregon is likely to return to the top 15 after falling out of the poll for four weeks.
 Who will move into the poll this week is a tricky question. The two teams ranked by the CFP but not the AP last week — Missouri and Oklahoma State — lost. The only other teams that received votes in the AP poll were Duke (lost to Miami), Liberty (beat MTSU), Louisville (beat UNC) and North Texas (lost to UTSA).
 Advertisement
 A five-game winning streak has Louisville 7-3 and likely to sneak back in. Liberty (9-1), UTSA (8-2) and Memphis (8-2) will get votes as well.
 The lack of obvious Top 25 contenders could mean that most of the teams at the bottom of the rankings that lost will hang onto spots, with some 6-4 teams, like Florida (which beat Kentucky), candidates to move in. One-point losses by Arizona and LSU to quality opponents could keep them from falling out.
 I’ll guess that South Carolina, New Mexico and SMU drop out and are replaced by Louisville, Liberty and Florida.
 Next week
 Week 12 has three matchups of teams ranked in last week’s AP poll. When the new rankings come out, it’s possible that number shrinks to as few as … zero.
 No. 1 Georgia at No. 20 South Carolina. The Gamecocks’ rising Playoff hopes ahead of welcoming No. 1 were shattered by a blowout loss at Arkansas.
 No. 24 LSU at No. 9 Tennessee. Lane Kiffin returning to Tennessee can’t help but be interesting.
 No. 25 SMU at No. 3 Notre Dame . The CFP stakes have diminished, with Notre Dame looking like a lock and the Mustangs’ chances all but gone after a blowout loss to Wake Forest.
 Elsewhere, both remaining undefeated teams hit the road: No. 2 Utah goes to TCU and No. 4 UCLA goes to Michigan. Rounding out the top five, No. 5 Miami hosts fading Virginia Tech.
 This story will be updated.
